verdict.rationale: Anrok's API docs say each product is assigned a product tax category (PTC) that determines its taxability in each jurisdiction. They also describe a mapping endpoint that creates many-to-1 mappings from billing-system products to Anrok products, so the core catalog-to-category mapping is first-party documented. However, the evidence never names which categories exist (SaaS, digital goods, services, physical products), and nothing independent or hands-on corroborates it. missing for 10: documented range of tax categories covering SaaS, digital goods, services and physical products; per-line-item taxability shown across every jurisdiction; independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can map my catalog to the vendor's tax categories — SaaS, digital goods, services, physical products — so each line item is taxed by what it is, in every jurisdiction it sells

citations.quote: Each product is identified by an external ID and is assigned a product tax category (PTC) which determines the product's taxability in each jurisdiction.
you can use this API endpoint to create many-to-1 mappings to associate various products in your billing system with equivalent products that have already been created in Anrok
Anrok sellers only need to create product IDs for each unique tax category, not every single product in the catalog.
